questionText: The dietary approach recommended in clinical nutrition for managing hypertension (DASH diet) emphasizes:

options.text: High potassium, calcium, magnesium, and dietary fiber with restricted sodium intake
High saturated animal fats and refined table sugar with zero dietary fiber
High sodium chloride intake with complete restriction of green vegetables
Exclusive consumption of red processed meats without water

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:

The DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, poultry, fish, and nuts, reducing sodium, red meats, sweets, and saturated fats to lower blood pressure.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: In pediatric clinical assessment, Kwashiorkor is clinically distinguished from Marasmus by the prominent presence of:

options.text: Severe muscle wasting and subcutaneous fat depletion without oedema (skin and bone appearance)
Oedema (fluid accumulation in legs and face) and enlarged fatty liver with adequate calorie intake but acute protein deficiency
Vitamin C scurvy bleeding gums exclusively
Excessive subcutaneous adipose tissue and childhood obesity

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Public Nutrition and Health - Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus):
Kwashiorkor is caused by acute protein deficiency despite sufficient caloric intake, leading to generalized oedema, enlarged fatty liver, lethargy, and a 'moon face'. Marasmus is total protein-energy malnutrition characterized by severe wasting without oedema.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:

chapter: Care and Maintenance of Fabrics in Institutions
questionText: When removing protein-based stains (such as blood or egg) from fabrics, one should strictly avoid using hot water because:

options.text: Hot water bleaches synthetic dyes instantly
Hot water coagulates the protein, setting the stain permanently into the fabric fibers
Protein stains dissolve only in boiling concentrated sulphuric acid
Hot water transforms the protein into insoluble cellulose wax

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Care and Maintenance of Fabrics in Institutions - Stain Removal: Protein Stains):
Protein coagulates when heated. Washing blood or egg stains with hot water 'cooks' the protein into the yarns, fixing it permanently. Protein stains must always be treated first with cold or lukewarm water and mild enzymatic detergent.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Read the following occupational ergonomics case study and answer the questions that follow:

An occupational health audit at an export garment manufacturing factory reveals alarming health complaints among 200 sewing machine operators. Over 70% of female machine stitchers suffer from chronic Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs): lower back pain, neck stiffness, shoulder impingement, and Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the wrists. An ergonomics expert inspects the workstations and identifies severe ergonomic design flaws:
1. Sewing chairs are rigid wooden stools without lumbar backrests, forcing operators into continuous forward-stooped static kyphotic postures.
2. Foot pedals are fixed at awkward high angles, straining ankle joints and impeding venous blood return.
3. Poor task illumination (dim, flickering tubes) creates severe visual glare and eye strain, forcing operators to crane their necks close to needles.
The factory management executes an ergonomic redesign: introducing adjustable ergonomic chairs with lumbar support, adjustable angled foot pedals, glare-free LED needle task lights, and instituting mandatory 3-minute hourly stretch breaks.

options.text: Increases ligament elasticity in joint capsules, permanently lengthens skeletal muscle fibers, and prevents structural joint degeneration.
Interrupts static muscle contractions, restores capillary blood circulation to fatigued tissues, clears lactic acid, and re-lubricates spinal discs.
Elevates arterial blood pressure in upper extremities, accelerates glycogen depletion in skeletal muscles, and stabilizes spinal alignment.
Suppresses autonomic nervous system activity, reduces basal metabolic rate during repetitive tasks, and prevents motor unit fatigue.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Work, Livelihood and Career (Ergonomic Stretch Breaks Physiology):
Interrupts static muscle contractions, restores capillary blood circulation to fatigued tissues, clears lactic acid, and re-lubricates spinal discs.

Detailed Context:
Micro-breaks relieve static intramuscular pressure, facilitating oxygenated blood perfusion and dissipating fatigue metabolites. Hence Option B is correct.

questionText:
Read the following occupational ergonomics case study and answer the questions that follow:

An occupational health audit at an export garment manufacturing factory reveals alarming health complaints among 200 sewing machine operators. Over 70% of female machine stitchers suffer from chronic Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs): lower back pain, neck stiffness, shoulder impingement, and Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the wrists. An ergonomics expert inspects the workstations and identifies severe ergonomic design flaws:
1. Sewing chairs are rigid wooden stools without lumbar backrests, forcing operators into continuous forward-stooped static kyphotic postures.
2. Foot pedals are fixed at awkward high angles, straining ankle joints and impeding venous blood return.
3. Poor task illumination (dim, flickering tubes) creates severe visual glare and eye strain, forcing operators to crane their necks close to needles.
The factory management executes an ergonomic redesign: introducing adjustable ergonomic chairs with lumbar support, adjustable angled foot pedals, glare-free LED needle task lights, and instituting mandatory 3-minute hourly stretch breaks.

Question: What primary ergonomic risk factors in the garment factory induced chronic Musculoskeletal Disorders among the machine operators?

options.text: Operators eating too much fresh fruit during lunch
Sustained awkward static postures, repetitive wrist-finger movements, lack of lumbar back support, and poorly designed workstations
Factory floors being painted green
Sewing machines using blue thread instead of white

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Work, Livelihood and Career (Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs) Etiology):
Sustained awkward static postures, repetitive wrist-finger movements, lack of lumbar back support, and poorly designed workstations

Detailed Context:
WMSDs stem from mechanical stress: static sustained muscle loading, repetitive motions, unadjusted heights, and lack of ergonomic support.
Hence Option B is correct.

questionText:
Read the following guidance and psychological counselling case study and answer the questions that follow:

Priya, a 17-year-old Class 12 student preparing for engineering entrance examinations, approaches the school guidance counsellor. She exhibits severe academic distress: chronic insomnia, panic attacks before mock tests, crying spells, and deep feelings of worthlessness. She expresses that her parents expect her to secure a top rank, and she catastrophizes: 'If I don't get into IIT, my entire life is destroyed.'
The counsellor implements a structured therapeutic protocol rooted in Carl Rogers' Person-Centred Counselling and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT):
1. Rapport Building: Providing unconditional positive regard, empathetic listening, and assuring Priya of strict confidentiality.
2. Exploration: Actively listening to Priya's fears without judgment, reflecting her emotions, and identifying her irrational cognitive distortions.
3. Cognitive Reframing: Guiding Priya to challenge her catastrophic 'all-or-nothing' thinking and reframe failure as a learning opportunity.
4. Relaxation Training: Teaching diaphragmatic deep-breathing and Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) to manage acute somatic panic.

options.text: Paranoid hallucination

Hence Option B is correct.
